title: Empty technician columns stay on the board with no way to hide them
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard" and "Jenny Wilson"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 and S1-644 led by Esther Howard, nothing led by Jenny Wilson):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer "ZZAUTOTEST Empty Tech" (add it with the Add button in the customer box if it does not exist; using it keeps this test's work orders apart from others at the location) and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
  6. Make sure the work orders you will drag have no shift on the Schedule for their lead technician (Schedule > check the technician's row). If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" prompt appears anyway, click Keep shifts.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Empty Tech so only this test's work orders show.
  4. Make sure Assigned to me is off.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  6. Find Jenny Wilson's column.
  7. Look through the toolbar, the column header and any menus for a control to hide empty columns.
  8. Drag the S1-644 card onto Jenny Wilson's column and let go.
  9. Read both column counts.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Jenny Wilson's column is on the board even though she leads no work orders.
  • There is no control anywhere to hide empty technician columns.
  • The card can be dropped on her column: Jenny Wilson now shows 1 and Esther Howard drops from 2 to 1.
  • While Assigned to me is on or when nothing matches the filters, other rules apply (checked in other cases).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-R9, S3-R21, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions 853901313 SQ-7 / DR-26.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R9: “Keep empty eligible technician columns visible as drop targets, except while Assigned to me is enabled (S3-N1), subject to S1-N1.”
  • S3-R21: “Do not offer a control to hide empty eligible technician columns.”
